lessons.title: Practice Modern C STL Algorithms
lessons.description: Modern C++ checkpoint: implement sortVector(std::vector<int>& vec) so it sorts the vector in place with std::sort over the [vec.begin(), vec.end()) iterator range. The test sorts {3, 1, 2} and checks the result.

tests.name: test_sort_vec

source.name: cppreference.com — std::sort — 'Sorts the elements in the target range [first, last)'

learning_objectives: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn, and sort a std vector in place with std sort.

exercises.question: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn, and sort a std vector in place with std sort.
hints: Read the one job this step is practicing.
The example is about Modern C STL Algorithms.
std::sort(items.begin(), items.end());
exercises.explanation: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn, and sort a std vector in place with std sort.

exercises.question: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn. For sort a std vector in place with std sort, which line sorts and reads the largest value?
hints: Compare each line with the example.
One line matches the example.
std::sort(items.begin(), items.end());
exercises.explanation: After sorting, back() is the largest value.

exercises.question: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn. For sort a std vector in place with std sort, what value is displayed?
hints: Run the example in your head from the top.
The last line is what gets displayed.
exercises.explanation: The Modern C STL Algorithms program displays that value.

exercises.question: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn. For sort a std vector in place with std sort, build the line that sorts and reads the largest value.
hints: Start at the left of the example.
Keep the example order.
std::vector<int> items{left, right}; std::sort(items.begin(), items.end());
exercises.explanation: After sorting, back() is the largest value.

exercises.question: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn. For sort a std vector in place with std sort, fill the blank so the line sorts and reads the largest value.
hints: The blank is the missing piece of the example.
The example uses that piece.
end()
exercises.explanation: After sorting, back() is the largest value.

exercises.question: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn. For sort a std vector in place with std sort, which line does a different job than the example?
hints: The other lines match the example.
One line is the odd one.
Line 8
exercises.explanation: The print reads the front before sorting, so it is not the largest.

exercises.question: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn. For sort a std vector in place with std sort, what does the second run display?
hints: Apply the same steps to the new value.
The display comes from the last line.
exercises.explanation: The second Modern C STL Algorithms program displays that value.

exercises.question: Harbor clerks recount crates before dawn. For sort a std vector in place with std sort, fill the blank so the program prints the result.
hints: The blank is the missing piece.
Print the value that piece produces.

exercises.explanation: The printed value is the result after this step sorts and reads the largest value.
